Case_Content:
Woman, 56 years old, right T3N1M1 colon cancer, four liver metastases (3-5 cm) at the thoraco-abdominal CT scan, CEA 780 ng/mL, non-V600E BRAF mutation (D594G).
MDT Discussion: Atypical BRAF mutation, intermediate prognosis, bilobar liver involvement.
Response:
Step 1 - Resectability assessment  
Potentially resectable  
 Four bilobar metastases measuring 3‑5 cm each are technically amenable to resection provided an adequate future liver remnant (FLR ≥ 30 % of total liver volume) can be preserved.  
 The disease is synchronous, CEA is markedly elevated (780 ng/mL) and the tumour harbours an atypical BRAF D594G mutation, all of which are adverse biologic factors that traditionally prompt a “proof‑of‑time” approach with neoadjuvant systemic therapy before committing to surgery.  
 Therefore a prerequisite action – neoadjuvant chemotherapy (with or without targeted agents) and reassessment of tumor response and FLR – is required before a definitive surgical plan can be made.

Step 2 - Oncological strategy  
 Induction systemic therapy – Begin 6 cycles of a triplet regimen (FOLFOXIRI) combined with an anti‑VEGF antibody (bevacizumab). The regimen is preferred for BRAF‑mutated mCRC to maximise response rates and to test tumour biology.  
 Restaging after induction – Repeat high‑resolution liver MRI with liver‑specific contrast and CT‑based volumetry to:  
  – Assess radiologic response of each metastasis (RECIST).  
  – Calculate FLR; if FLR < 30 % consider portal vein embolisation (PVE) or associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS).  
 Surgical sequencing –  
  – If FLR is sufficient after response, proceed with a liver‑first (reverse) approach: perform hepatic resection first (either single‑stage major hepatectomy or two‑stage/ALPPS depending on lesion distribution).  
  – If FLR is marginal, perform PVE, wait 4–6 weeks, then re‑image and proceed with staged hepatectomy.  
  – After completion of liver surgery and recovery, perform definitive resection of the primary right‑sided colon tumour (right hemicolectomy) either simultaneously (if liver resection is limited) or in a second operation, guided by intra‑operative findings and patient fitness.  
 Adjuvant/maintenance therapy – Resume systemic therapy post‑operatively to complete a total of 12 months of chemotherapy (including the induction cycles). Consider adding a BRAF‑directed agent (e.g., encorafenib + cetuximab) in the adjuvant setting if the mutation is confirmed to be functionally activating and the patient tolerates it, ideally within a clinical trial.  
 Surveillance – Serial CEA measurements and imaging (CT or MRI) every 3–4 months for the first 2 years, then every 6 months up to 5 years.

Step 3 - Missing data  
 Performance status (ECOG) and detailed comorbidity profile (ASA/Charlson).  
 Baseline liver function tests (bilirubin, AST/ALT, INR, albumin) and assessment of chemotherapy‑induced hepatotoxicity risk.  
 Precise volumetric data: total liver volume and calculated future liver remnant.  
 Detailed anatomic relationship of each metastasis to major vascular structures (portal vein, hepatic veins, hepatic artery).  
 KRAS/NRAS status (to confirm wild‑type and guide anti‑EGFR use).  
 Microsatellite instability / dMMR status (relevant for immunotherapy considerations).  
 Confirmation that there are no extra‑hepatic metastases (lung, peritoneum, lymph nodes) on staging CT/PET.  
 Patient’s preference regarding surgical timing and willingness to undergo intensive chemotherapy.

The presence of a non-V600E BRAF D594G mutation is associated with a more indolent biology compared with V600E and does not contraindicate surgical intent. • Perform high-resolution liver MRI and contrast-enhanced CT to define precise vascular and biliary relationships of all lesions.

• Perform high-quality liver MRI after 2-3 months to evaluate response.

• If disease remains controlled, perform ultrasound-guided parenchymal-sparing resections of all four lesions.

• Pathology report : confirmation of tumor type and origin, immunohistochemistry with tumor markers, histological growth pattern, margin status (R0, R1, R2), tumor grade, differentiation, pathologic response score (TRG), necrosis/fibrosis

Case_Content:
Man, 65 years old, left T4N2M1 colon cancer, six liver metastases (2-4 cm)at the thoraco-abdominal CT scan, CEA 320 ng/mL, RAS wild-type, MSS. Positive circulating tumor cells detected.
MDT Discussion: Presence of circulating tumor cells despite no visible extension, prognostic value discussed.
Response:
Step 1 – Resectability assessment  
Potentially resectable  
- Six liver metastases (2‑4 cm) are not an absolute contraindication, but the current imaging does not provide:  
  • precise segmental distribution (unilateral vs bilateral)  
  • relationship to major vascular/biliary structures  
  • calculated future liver remnant (FLR) volume  
- The disease is synchronous, CEA is markedly elevated (320 ng/mL) and circulating tumor cells are positive, indicating aggressive biology; guidelines recommend “proof of time” with systemic therapy before committing to surgery.  
- Therefore a prerequisite systemic (neoadjuvant) treatment phase and additional volumetric imaging are required before a definitive surgical plan can be made.  

Step 2 – Oncological strategy  
1. Induction systemic therapy  
   - Start 6 cycles of a doublet or triplet regimen (e.g., FOLFOXIRI) combined with an anti‑EGFR antibody (cetuximab or panitumumab) because the tumour is RAS‑wild‑type and MSS.  
   - Aim for maximal tumour shrinkage and to assess disease biology (response, CTC clearance).  

2. Restaging after induction  
   - Perform high‑resolution liver MRI with hepatobiliary contrast plus CT of chest/abdomen to:  
     • Re‑evaluate number, size and location of liver lesions  
     • Calculate FLR (target ≥30 % of total liver volume or >0.5 % / kg body weight)  
   - Repeat CEA and circulating tumor cell assay; a decline supports favorable biology.  

3. Decision point  
   - If imaging shows adequate FLR and all lesions are resectable with negative margins → proceed to curative‑intent liver surgery.  
   - If FLR is insufficient → consider portal vein embolisation (PVE) or associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS) to induce hypertrophy, followed by re‑assessment.  
   - If disease remains extensive or progresses → continue systemic therapy, possibly switch to second‑line regimen, and reassess for conversion or enrolment in a clinical trial.  

4. Surgical sequencing  
   - Because the primary tumour is T4N2, schedule a curative resection of the colon primary (segmental left colectomy with adequate lymphadenectomy) either before or concurrently with liver surgery, depending on intra‑operative assessment and patient fitness.  
   - Aim for R0 resection of all hepatic lesions; use intra‑operative ultrasound to detect occult disease.  
   - If a single‑stage hepatectomy would leave inadequate FLR, adopt a two‑stage approach:  
     a. First stage – resect lesions in the future liver remnant (e.g., left lateral section) and perform PVE of the right portal branch.  
     b. After 4–6 weeks of hypertrophy, complete right‑hemi hepatectomy (or extended resection) to clear remaining disease.  

5. Peri‑operative systemic therapy  
   - After surgery, administer adjuvant chemotherapy (e.g., 3–6 months of the same regimen) unless postoperative pathology shows complete response and patient recovers well, in which case a shorter course may be considered.  

6. Follow‑up  
   - Serial CEA, imaging (CT/MRI) every 3–4 months for the first 2 years, then every 6 months, and periodic CTC monitoring as a research/prognostic tool.  

Step 3 – Missing data  
- Detailed liver volumetry (FLR calculation) and segmental location of each metastasis.  
- Vascular/biliary involvement of the lesions (proximity to hepatic veins, portal pedicles, bile ducts).  
- Performance status (ECOG), comorbidities, and baseline liver function (bilirubin, INR, platelets).  
- Full staging of extra‑hepatic sites (chest CT, PET‑CT) to exclude occult lung or peritoneal disease.  
- Quantitative circulating tumor cell count and trend after systemic therapy.  
- Patient’s preferences regarding the intensity of treatment and willingness for staged hepatic surgery.
